Something has definitely changed here: news about what is happening in America has become so common that our body is in India, but our mind is slowly being pulled toward America.

The question is not whether the market in America is growing because of AI and the market in India is falling because of a lack of technology.

The question is: Why are we still behind in technology?
Why have we been doing nothing but copying for years?

Why is it not the other way around—why doesn’t America copy us?

What is lacking in our education system?
What is lacking in our government policies?

Why don’t we have our own AI?
Why don’t we have our own Meta?

Where is the weakness?

How long will we continue praising others while constantly criticizing ourselves?

First, the Mughals ruled over us, and then the British ruled over us.

Today, America is ruling us—mentally or technologically.

Why is this happening?

Because education is not given the importance it deserves in our country.

If someone talks about education or rules and discipline, instead of supporting them, people try to pull them down.

If someone talks about changing something in the system or creating something new, they are discouraged by saying:

“We are all living normal lives. How can you be the only one talking about such things?”

Because we simply do not want to grow.

We are content to see others moving ahead while seeing ourselves as weak, and then spend our lives carrying these feelings.

Perhaps we have become accustomed to thousands of years of being ruled by others.

When will the day come when America, China, Russia, Japan, and all the other developed countries talk about our civilization and our technology?

In our country, the highest respect and recognition seem to be reserved for powerful politicians, political leaders, and ministers.

The people who are among the most educated in our country, who are working for science and technology, who are exceptionally intelligent, and who are contributing across the world—why are they rarely discussed?

Why not?

Something has definitely changed here: news about what is happening in America has become so common that our body is in India, but our mind is slowly being pulled toward America.

The question is not whether the market in America is growing because of AI and the market in India is falling because of a lack of technology.

The question is: Why are we still behind in technology?
Why have we been doing nothing but copying for years?

Why is it not the other way around—why doesn’t America copy us?

What is lacking in our education system?
What is lacking in our government policies?

Why don’t we have our own AI?
Why don’t we have our own Meta?

Where is the weakness?

How long will we continue praising others while constantly criticizing ourselves?

First, the Mughals ruled over us, and then the British ruled over us.

Today, America is ruling us—mentally or technologically.

Why is this happening?

Because education is not given the importance it deserves in our country.

If someone talks about education or rules and discipline, instead of supporting them, people try to pull them down.

If someone talks about changing something in the system or creating something new, they are discouraged by saying:

“We are all living normal lives. How can you be the only one talking about such things?”

Because we simply do not want to grow.

We are content to see others moving ahead while seeing ourselves as weak, and then spend our lives carrying these feelings.

Perhaps we have become accustomed to thousands of years of being ruled by others.

When will the day come when America, China, Russia, Japan, and all the other developed countries talk about our civilization and our technology?

In our country, the highest respect and recognition seem to be reserved for powerful politicians, political leaders, and ministers.

The people who are among the most educated in our country, who are working for science and technology, who are exceptionally intelligent, and who are contributing across the world—why are they rarely discussed?

Why not?
